description: Opt-in overlay for repositories where a person reviews dependency updates but should not tick them one by one: minor, patch and pin updates share one pull request that opens without a dashboard tick and waits for a human merge, after a release-age soak. Digests are left to safe-automerge, majors keep the tick. Extend after the default preset.

packageRules.description: Minor, patch and pin updates share one branch and open without a dashboard tick. One pull request per run instead of one per dependency: every open branch costs a CI run each time it is rebased. A branch that waits for a person rebases only on a conflict: with behind-base-branch every push to the base branch would rebase it and rerun its CI. Branches that merge themselves set behind-base-branch, because a red result from an old base would otherwise keep them from merging forever.
Without the tick the soak returns, so a freshly published release is not proposed the hour it appears.
One pull request per package and repository bumps every pin of that package together (apm.yml and the agentstd tag in mise.toml), so the generated files and the lockfile move in one step.
Skills from webgrip/ai-skills share one branch: each skill is its own dependency, and one branch per skill would make every other skill branch conflict on apm.lock.yaml once the first merges.

Shared preset bumps merge themselves once the pull request checks are green: no dashboard tick, no release-age soak, their own branch. The preset is Webgrip's own reviewed code, released from this repository, and every consumer waiting for a tick on it is a policy fix that has not landed. Renovate's automerge, not the platform's, so a branch without checks does not merge at once. It is never digest-pinned: It is already pinned to a protected semver release tag; the global pinDigests=true otherwise makes Renovate try to rewrite 'local>webgrip/renovate-config#vX.Y.Z' to a commit SHA, the replacement never applies ('Digest is not updated'), and the whole pin-dependencies branch aborts with 'Error updating branch: update failure' on every run. A preset bump changes how Renovate treats the repository, not what it ships, so it lands as chore(renovate) and never cuts a release.. The generator appends this part to every preset it builds, so no grouping, soak or commit-type rule of an earlier part can catch the bump.
